name: Market Surveillance Regulation
evidence_rating: thin: one partial Commission report on Article 4 based on authority surveys; full evaluation (due July 2026) not found; no independent studies
summary: The Regulation strengthened checks on products sold in the EU, including a rule that every product must have an EU-based responsible company. A 2025 Commission review found no clear improvement in compliance: about one in ten checked products still fails the rules, and in an online check only a third of the EU contacts given could be confirmed. Meanwhile direct imports of cheap parcels tripled to 4.6 billion in 2024, and the full evaluation is still awaited.

indicators.indicator: Compliance rates by Member State/sector, for e-commerce and imports
indicators.evidence: Partial: authorities report non-compliance in about 10% of checks (11% in 2019, 9% in 2022), 12% for products under Article 4; no EU-wide compliance-rate series. Commission reports 4.6bn low-value parcels imported in 2024, straining controls.

indicators.indicator: Number of coordinated control campaigns and results
indicators.evidence: Joint actions run through the Union Product Compliance Network (e.g. 2023 online check of 215 offers); no aggregate count found.

indicators.indicator: Use of mutual assistance mechanisms and replicated measures
indicators.evidence: Not reported in available documents; full evaluation (due July 2026) not found.

indicators.indicator: Awareness/understanding of product rules by businesses
indicators.evidence: Very low economic operator response to the Article 4 study survey; no measure.

indicators.indicator: Products sold in the EU must have an EU-based responsible economic operator
indicators.evidence: Article 4 report: operator missing in 7% of checks and wrong in 5%; in a 2023 online joint action only 34% of indicated operators could be confirmed; half of authorities saw no change in compliance and none clearly attributable.

indicators.indicator: Union Product Compliance Network about EUR 18m a year

literature.citation: European Commission (2017), Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal on compliance with and enforcement of Union harmonisation legislation on products (executive summary SWD(2017) 467), SWD(2017) 466
literature.title: Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal on compliance with and enforcement of Union harmonisation legislation on products (executive summary SWD(2017) 467)
literature.headline: Products under EU harmonised rules worth over EUR 2,400bn a year (69% of manufactured output); expected fewer non-compliant products, more efficient import checks and a level playing field; EU Product Compliance Network costs about EUR 18m a year
literature.summary_plain: The Commission expected stronger, better coordinated market surveillance to reduce unsafe and non-compliant products, without quantifying the gain.

literature.citation: European Commission (2025), Report on the implementation of Article 4 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020, COM(2025) 63
literature.title: Report on the implementation of Article 4 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020
literature.method: review (survey of 108 market surveillance authorities, joint actions, evaluation study)
literature.headline: 85% of authorities checked Article 4; operator absent in 7% and incorrect in 5% of checks; only 34% of indicated operators confirmed in a 2023 online joint action; non-compliance about 10% of checks with no clear change; half of authorities saw no change; not a full evaluation
literature.summary_plain: A Commission review found the rule requiring an EU-based contact for products has had no clear effect on compliance yet, and online sellers often give wrong details.
literature.quality: partial report; survey-based; low business response

literature.citation: European Commission (2025), A comprehensive EU toolbox for safe and sustainable e-commerce, COM(2025) 37
literature.title: A comprehensive EU toolbox for safe and sustainable e-commerce
literature.headline: 4.6bn low-value consignments imported in 2024, nearly double 2023 (2.4bn) and more than triple 2022 (1.4bn); surge of non-compliant products strains authorities; calls for stronger enforcement
literature.summary_plain: The Commission says direct imports of cheap parcels tripled in two years to 4.6 billion in 2024, overwhelming product checks.
literature.quality: context, not an evaluation of the Regulation

literature.title: Large scale EU customs control action shows most third-country e-commerce goods do not follow standards (results of priority control area action and product compliance controls report 2022-2024)
literature.venue: European Commission, Taxation and Customs Union news, 7 January 2026
literature.method: EU-wide customs priority control action (20,000 toys and small electronics checked, sample lab-tested) plus Member State statistics on customs product-compliance controls under Art. 25 of Regulation 2019/1020, 2022-2024
literature.outcomes: non-compliance of imported e-commerce goods; customs interventions and refusals
literature.headline: More than half of 20,000 checked e-commerce toys and small electronics did not meet EU standards and 84% of lab-tested items were dangerous, while customs refused on average only 13 items per million released in 2024 as controls lag e-commerce growth.
literature.summary_plain: Border checks show most cheap products shipped directly to EU shoppers break EU safety rules, but customs can only stop a tiny fraction of the billions of parcels arriving.
literature.quality: Official monitoring data; targeted (risk-based) sample so non-compliance not representative; underlying report not opened, read via Commission news page
literature.interested_party: Commission reporting on its own framework
literature.citation: European Commission (DG TAXUD) (2026), Large scale EU customs control action shows most third-country e-commerce goods do not follow standards (results of priority control area action and product compliance controls report 2022-2024), European Commission, Taxation and Customs Union news, 7 January 2026
